Pest's `uses()` helper is directory-based.

A probe test will be written in `/tmp` with an explicit `uses(TestCase::class)` call, since the repository sandbox blocks writes.

The TestCase sets `vaulter`.

The test suite disables auth middleware and relies on `actingAs`. The permission driver defaults to null but is switched to database by `V1::drive`. I will write a probe using `actingAs` user 2 to verify the route behavior.

The uniform not found dataset omits `files.revisions.store`. The existing `IfMatchRequiredTest` confirms that invisible users receive 404 instead of 428 for this route.

The uniform test compares response bodies, but the dedicated `IfMatchRequiredTest` only asserts a 404 status for `files.revisions.store`. A body mismatch there would be missed. The drive existence oracle remains the primary finding.

I am probing additional routes: POST folders with parent on known versus unknown drives, GET nodes with a parent query, POST uploads with node_id, POST files with parent_id, and DELETE trash. I also checked whether revisions.store could return 422 for missing multipart file before 404; if both cases yield the same status code, this is not a leak.

Node ID routes for unknown versus invisible nodes are covered by the uniform test. Both cases resolve to the same `NodeNotFound` exception type and identical response bodies, so no leak exists there.

The leak is specific to drive-id-in-URL routes that resolve the parent drive before the child node. P6-I2 explicitly lists this as a threat: different `drive_not_found` codes for foreign tenants. Here the violation is within the same tenant, where an invisible drive returns 403 while an unknown drive returns 404. The parent probe distinguishes these two cases.

The severity is major. This is a violation of the access-boundary invariant P6-I2, which forbids leaking drive existence through different HTTP codes. It is not a data exfiltration bug, but it is an existence oracle the design explicitly prohibits. The guessability of drive IDs does not change this assessment.

POST uploads and files without a parent are safe because they resolve the drive before checking the child node. The leak is limited to routes that accept a parent_id or query parameter.

DELETE trash returns 200 for an invisible drive but 404 for an unknown drive. This deviation is already recorded and will not be reported again.

Search 200 versus 404 is also a recorded deviation and not a new finding.

The `GET nodes?parent={rootId}` route leaks even when the parent is the real root of an invisible drive. The controller authorizes View on that parent, so an invisible root returns NodeNotFound while an unknown drive returns drive_not_found. This distinction holds even if the attacker does not know the root ID.

I will reproduce this leak and also check empty trash and folders in the same probe.

I will also test whether a feature gate on an invisible parent returns 404 instead of 403. I plan to run TrashV1Test, IfMatch tests, and the uniform suite alongside my probe to verify etag consistency. I am checking RoleRegistry for the correct reader role name so I can probe the ability-before-If-Match ordering.
The trash ETag from listing works for purge. The test expects a 204 response.

I will write and run a probe test.

Running existing tests first to rule out environmental failures. The probe uses Pest syntax and TestCase with RefreshDatabase. User 1 gets owner access via V1::drive. User 2 has no grant. I will check reader role responses for 428 versus 403.

ShowAbilitiesController calls abilities() before explain(). The former needs only View. The latter needs Manage. This ordering is correct.

Invalid explain values return 422 before any node lookup, preventing leaks. located() in explain() also enforces the same View-then-Manage check.

I will write and run a probe to verify that readers get 428. I also noticed a potential issue: `children()` is scoped to the handle's drive, but the URL may contain a different drive ID. In that case, the locator would find no node, returning `node_not_found`.

I will also probe uploads and files. Files can be tested with UploadedFile::fake(). I suspect a second bug: onDrive may convert NodeNotFound from a name conflict or sibling during root upload into drive_not_found.

Duplicate root uploads return 409, not the suspected drive_not_found. The drive_not_found conversion only occurs when a child ID is supplied. I will also probe POST folders without parent and DELETE trash to confirm uniform behavior.

The review brief seam 2 requires the If-Match check before the View permission, but the design places the ability check first. This contradicts the Validators order and could be a minor defect if the author missed it.

The item rule requires `requireIfMatch` before `find`, but the implementation finds the node first and calls `matchNode` only after. This is safer than the item rule and matches P6-I1. The design still places the ability check before If-Match, so the implementation does not follow that specific ordering. I will report this as a minor finding if reproduced.

I will write a comprehensive probe.

The feature gate only hides the target node ID. The drive ID still leaks because the drive resolves before the feature check. This raises a question about which IDs the brief intends to protect.

The code comment clarifies that the feature gate hides target and upload session IDs. Resolving the drive before the feature check leaks its existence, but this occurs even when the feature is enabled. The probe now distinguishes between node_id and onDrive paths when the feature is disabled.

The drive-existence oracle is separate from the feature gate. The probe targets child-qualified routes for this leak. The existing test only covers routes without a child ID, so it misses the parent oracle path.

The child-id routes use forDrive(), confirming the drive exists before checking the child. This is a legitimate finding, not the recorded list behavior. Severity is calibrated as Information: it reveals only drive existence, requires authentication, uses different problem codes, and violates explicit invariant P6-I2. The project's own test defines an invisible drive as an unreadable root and checks uniformity only for routes without a child parameter.

The test configuration uses sequential bigint drive IDs. This makes the drive-existence oracle trivially enumerable: a caller can scan small integers and observe the difference between `drive_not_found` and `node_not_found`. Severity is raised to Major. The probe will reproduce this enumeration.

I will also check POST drives/{id}/folders with a parent and whether meta routes leak drive existence. I plan to run the revisions.restore test to confirm that node-level routes do not have the same bug.

ContentResponder direct_signed opens nothing before checks. This is acceptable.

Tus HEAD returns 204 instead of the design table's 200. Tests lock in this behavior. It is a minor pre-existing contract mismatch.

The 204 HEAD status is part of this diff, so it will be included in the report. The s3 versus s3-multipart protocol distinction is not a defect because UPGRADE documents s3-multipart and the enum is pre-existing. I am now writing the probe and running the relevant Http tests in parallel.

The full Http suite will run alongside the probe. Drive Http tests come first because that is where the bug lives. The probe file is at /tmp/p67-probe.php and uses Pest's `uses()` helper.

The probe file needs both `RefreshDatabase` and the base `TestCase` trait. The existing Http suite already applies `RefreshDatabase` to its test files, but this standalone probe sits outside that group and must include both imports explicitly.

The probe helper cannot access `$this` inside a closure, so the test will use a direct `V1::drive()` call to obtain a real drive ID. It then builds cases comparing an unknown drive path against an invisible one when a child ID is supplied.

The probe now includes POST routes for folders, uploads, and files. File creation requires a fake multipart upload because `postJson` cannot send binary data.

VERDICT: FINDINGS

## 1. major — `packages/drive/src/Http/Controllers/Nodes/ListChildrenController.php:31`

A drive the caller cannot see is distinguishable from a drive that does not exist, as soon as the route carries a child id (`parent`, `parent_id`, or `node_id`). `HttpResourceResolver::drive()` returns the row before any visibility check. The child lookup then fails as `node_not_found`. An unknown drive id fails earlier as `drive_not_found`. P6-I2 requires those two answers to match except for `request_id`. `UniformNotFoundDriveV1Test` only covers the no-parent routes, which do match.

The same split is in `CreateFolderController.php:26`, `UploadFileController.php:31`, and `CreateUploadController.php:49`. Root-relative calls (no child id) stay uniform. Turning resumable uploads off does not close it: the drive is resolved before the feature gate. Search and `DELETE …/trash` returning 200 to a stranger are the recorded P6.7 deviation and are separate from this.

**Reproduction.** User 1 owns the drive; user 2 has no grant. SQLite in memory, `permission_driver=database`.

| Request | Existing drive | Unknown drive |
|---|---|---|
| `GET drives/{id}/nodes?parent=no-such` | 404 `node_not_found` | 404 `drive_not_found` |
| `POST drives/{id}/folders` `{name, parent_id: no-such}` | 404 `node_not_found` | 404 `drive_not_found` |
| `POST drives/{id}/files` with `parent_id` | 404 `node_not_found` | 404 `drive_not_found` |
| `POST drives/{id}/uploads` with `parent_id` or `node_id` | 404 `node_not_found` | 404 `drive_not_found` |
| same upload with `vaulter-drive.uploads.resumable.enabled=false` | 404 `node_not_found` | 404 `drive_not_found` |
| `GET drives/{id}/nodes` (no parent) | 404 `drive_not_found` | 404 `drive_not_found` |
| `POST` folder / file / upload with no child id | 404 `drive_not_found` | 404 `drive_not_found` |

A caller who can see the named parent still has to get that page. Only the miss (unknown or invisible child) must not use a different code from an unknown drive.

## 2. minor — `packages/drive/src/Http/Controllers/Nodes/UpdateNodeController.php:21`

On every IM route, `expectedSequence()` runs after View and before the mutation ability. P6-design#Validators requires the missing ability to be 403 before If-Match. A reader (View, no Edit) is told about the precondition first:

- no `If-Match` → 428 `precondition_required`
- `If-Match: *` → 428 `precondition_required`
- `If-Match: "not-the-tag"` → 412 `node_sequence_mismatch` (`meta` is `node_id` only; the current tag is not in the body)
- `If-Match` equal to the GET tag → 403 `permission_denied`

The name stayed `r.txt`. The same 428 happens for `POST nodes/{id}/trash`. View still precedes 428, so an invisible node stays 404.

`HEAD uploads/{upload}` returns 204. The P6.7 route table and the tus 1.0.0 HEAD rule both say 200. No deviation is recorded. `tests/Feature/TusResponseContractsTest.php` passed here, including `assertNoContent()` on that HEAD (204), with `Tus-Resumable`, `Upload-Length`, and `Cache-Control: no-store, private`.
